question: Should OpenClaw support workflow completion automation through a new internal `session:end` hook event, or declare the typed plugin `session_end` hook as the supported replacement for this use case?
rationale: Current main has a real plugin lifecycle hook but not the requested internal hook, and VISION.md prefers plugin surfaces unless a core/API gap remains.

options.title: Bless plugin `session_end`
options.body: Document the plugin hook as the supported completion signal for workflow integrations and close or narrow this internal-hook request if it covers the use case.

options.title: Add internal `session:end`
options.body: Define a typed internal event and wire it through session completion paths when maintainers want `HOOK.md` scripts, not plugins, to own this automation contract.

options.title: Defer to linked PR review
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 and the related session-memory reports are resolved, then reassess the remaining hook boundary.

recommendation.title: Bless plugin `session_end`
recommendation.body: Document the plugin hook as the supported completion signal for workflow integrations and close or narrow this internal-hook request if it covers the use case.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to recent hooks docs and gateway reset-hook review history, and the related pull request explicitly routes hooks/plugins review to him.
